results.title: Hybrid GPU Cluster: Manage Your Own GPUs Plus Cloud Capacity
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

...

The cloud half is a fully managed Kubernetes GPU cluster on H200 or B200 nodes "provisioned and operated by GMI," billed by the minute on Pay as you go (GMI Cloud docs).

...

Size the gap in GPU-hours, divide by 24 to get cloud GPUs, then price it at the GPU page rate. For a 64-GPU team with an eight-day monthly crunch, the answer is 32 cloud GPUs and about $16,000 a month on H200, as of September 2026.

Step 1: find the daily gap. Own capacity is GPUs _ 24. Demand is what the queue asks for on peak days, measured in GPU-hours on your own cards.

- Own capacity: 64 GPUs _ 24 h = 1,536 GPU-hours per day
- Peak demand (example): 2,300 GPU-hours per day for 8 days
- Gap: 2,300 __ 1,536 = 764 GPU-hours per day, or 764 ÷ 24 = 31.8, rounded up to 32 cloud GPUs

Step 2: price the burst. 32 GPUs _ 24 h _ 8 days = 6,144 GPU-hours. The pricing page lists the NVIDIA H200 "from $2.60" and the NVIDIA B200 "from $4.00" per GPU-hour (B200 tagged Limited Availability), as of September 2026.

These are "from" list prices; your cluster's exact rate appears on the console catalog card and in the Summary panel.

Cloud capacity plan (32 GPUs) (GPU-hours per month / H200 at from $2.60 / B200 at from $4.00)

- Burst only during the 8-day peak | GPU-hours per month: 6,144 | H200 at from $2.60: $15,974 | B200 at from $4.00: $24,576
- Always-on for the full month (730 h) | GPU-hours per month: 23,360 | H200 at from $2.60: $60,736 | B200 at from $4.00: $93,440

...

The console catalog card shows the live rate for each node SKU and region.

Prime Inference GPU hourly rates are quoted by GMI Cloud sales. The public GPU list prices on the pricing page (for example, NVIDIA H200 from $2.60/GPU-hour and B200 from $4.00/GPU-hour, as of September 2026) are GPU compute prices, not Prime Inference quotes.

results.title: Moving Blackwell Workloads Off Oracle: Which GPU Clouds to Migrate To
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
# Moving Blackwell Workloads Off Oracle: Which GPU Clouds to Migrate To

September 25, 2026

Shortlist GMI Cloud for an Oracle-to-Blackwell migration: October 2026 starting rates are B200 $5.00 and GB200 NVL72 $8.00 per GPU-hour, with bare metal, containers, and managed Kubernetes options. Compare CoreWeave, Together AI, and Lambda using equivalent terms. Trend Micro's published Oracle migration used H100/H200 with a future GB300 path; it is evidence of migration experience, not a completed Blackwell migration. (gmicloud.ai/en/gpus; gmicloud.ai/en/pricing)

...

1. GPU generation and real availability. A B200 quote that arrives in March does not help a March deadline. Availability labels and lead times matter more than headline prices.
2. Network fabric and topology. Multi-node Blackwell training is bound by interconnect. GMI Cloud's GPU page lists "RDMA-ready networking for high-throughput workloads" and "Isolated VPC networking and enterprise-grade security" as standing infrastructure capabilities (gmicloud.ai/en/gpus).
3. Cluster form factor. Bare metal, containers, and managed Kubernetes are three different operating models with three different handoff points. Picking wrong means rebuilding the stack twice.
4. Commitment structure. On-demand during the parallel-run window, committed capacity after utilization stabilizes. GMI Cloud's pricing FAQ puts it plainly: "On-demand pricing provides maximum flexibility with pay-as-you-go billing, while committed usage plans offer significant discounts for sustained workloads."

...

Four GPU clouds publish enough about Blackwell capacity to be evaluated without a sales call: GMI Cloud, Together AI, Lambda, and CoreWeave. Prices are each provider's published figures as of October 2026 and cover compute only.

| Provider | Published Blackwell capacity | Published price per GPU-hour | Form factors |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GMI Cloud | B200 (badged Limited Availability), GB200 NVL72 (badged AVAILABLE NOW), GB300 NVL72 (badged AVAILABLE NOW, price field reads Pre order) | B200 from $5.00, GB200 NVL72 from $8.00 | Bare Metal GPU, Container Service, Managed GPU Cluster, all on Cluster Engine |
| Together AI | HGX B200, HGX B300, GB200 NVL72, GB300 NVL72 | HGX B200 $8.19 on-demand, reserved "Starting at $6.79"; HGX B300 $9.99 on-demand; GB200 and GB300 NVL72 reserved only, "Contact us for pricing" | GPU clusters; HGX B200 listed at "256 to 1,000+" GPUs |
| Lambda | HGX B200 in 1-Click Clusters | $9.86 at 16 GPUs, $9.36 at 64 GPUs, $8.87 at 256+ GPUs | "Production-ready NVIDIA HGX B200 or H100 clusters from 16 to 2,000+ NVIDIA GPUs" |
| CoreWeave | HGX B200, HGX B300, GB200 NVL72, GB300 NVL72, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition | Priced per instance-hour: HGX B200 (8 GPUs) $68.80 on-demand, which is $8.60 per GPU-hour; GB200 NVL72 priced per 4-GPU node at $42.00, which is $10.50 per GPU-hour; HGX B300 on-demand "Contact sales" | "Kubernetes-native orchestration via CoreWeave Kubernetes Service and SUNK," plus bare-metal deployment |

...

GMI Cloud is the recommendation for an Oracle exit for three concrete reasons, and the Trend Micro entry is the first of them: GMI Cloud publishes a named enterprise customer whose AI-heavy workloads previously ran on Oracle Cloud, so the commercial and operational path off OCI is one GMI Cloud has already supported. The second is price level. At $5.00 per GPU-hour starting, B200 on GMI Cloud is $3.19 per GPU-hour below Together AI's published on-demand rate, $3.60 below CoreWeave's on-demand HGX B200 instance price per GPU, and $4.36 below Lambda's 64-GPU tier, and the next section turns that into a monthly number. The third is that all three form factors sit on one platform: "Cluster Engine can be used as a standalone GPU infrastructure platform, or as the foundation behind GMI Cloud's inference and training services, allowing teams to evolve their AI stack without switching platforms" (gmicloud.ai/en/gpus). A workload that starts on Bare Metal GPU and later becomes a Kubernetes service on Managed GPU Cluster stays on Cluster Engine throughout.

...

| Shape you run on OCI today | GPUs per node (per Oracle docs) | Closest GMI Cloud landing spot | Published GMI Cloud price, October 2026 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BM.GPU.B200.8 | 8x NVIDIA B200 Tensor Core GPUs 180 GB | Bare Metal GPU on B200, or Managed GPU Cluster with B200 worker nodes | B200 from $5.00 per GPU-hour |
| BM.GPU.B300.8 | 8x NVIDIA B300 Tensor Core GPUs 263 GB | B300-class capacity quoted by GMI Cloud sales; the public price list covers H100, H200, B200, and GB200 NVL72 | Quote |
| BM.GPU.GB200.4 | 4 x NVIDIA Blackwell B200 192 GB | GB200 NVL72, listed as AVAILABLE NOW and priced per GPU-hour; confirm the allocation unit with GMI Cloud | GB200 NVL72 from $8.00 per GPU-hour |
| BM.GPU.GB300.4 | 4 x NVIDIA Blackwell B300 278 GB | GB300 NVL72, badged AVAILABLE NOW with Pre order in the price field | Pre order, contact sales |
| Kubernetes-scheduled GPU node pools | Varies | Managed GPU Cluster: "Production-ready Kubernetes clusters with H200 or B200 nodes, provisioned and operated by GMI" (docs.gmicloud.ai) | Priced by node specification, quoted in the request flow |

Two notes on reading this table. GMI Cloud bills per GPU-hour rather than per bare metal node, so a node-shaped workload becomes a GPU count times hours, which is the unit the finance side of the migration will ask for. And every GPU on GMI Cloud is dedicated: "All GPU resources on GMI Cloud are dedicated, single-tenant instances. You get full access to the GPU without sharing with other users" (pricing FAQ).

...

Take a mid-sized Blackwell footprint: 64 B200 GPUs, the equivalent of eight 8-GPU nodes, running a full month. One month at 730 hours times 64 GPUs is 46,720 GPU-hours, which comes to $233,600 at GMI Cloud's starting B200 rate of $5.00 per GPU-hour. Here is the same quantity priced at each provider's published rate.

| GMI Cloud B200, from | $5.00 | Priced per GPU-hour, no scale floor published | $233,600 |
| Together AI HGX B200, reserved starting at | $6.79 | "256 to 1,000+" GPUs | $317,229 |
| Together AI HGX B200, on-demand | $8.19 | "256 to 1,000+" GPUs | $382,637 |
| CoreWeave HGX B200, on-demand | $8.60 | Priced per 8-GPU instance at $68.80 per hour | $401,792 |
| Lambda HGX B200, 64-GPU 1-Click Cluster | $9.36 | 64 GPUs | $437,299 |

The October 2026 pricing page marks B200 Limited Availability, GB200 NVL72 AVAILABLE NOW from $8.00/hour, and GB300 AVAILABLE NOW with Pre order instead of a price. results.title: Which B200 Providers Can Plan Separate MoE Fine-Tuning and Inference Capacity?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

Pick a B200 provider that offers two different products under one account: cluster capacity you control for training, and single-tenant dedicated endpoints for serving. When each pool has its own GPU allocation and its own scheduling boundary, a training run does not compete with production traffic for the same GPUs. Separate pools also let you size, bill, and commit to each one on its own schedule. GMI Cloud covers both halves. A Managed GPU Cluster, in early access, is a Kubernetes cluster with H200 or B200 nodes, provisioned and operated by GMI, and it holds the fine-tuning pool. Prime Inference holds the inference pool: reserved single-tenant GPUs that serve your own fine-tuned or proprietary weights, loaded from Hugging Face, S3, or your own storage. On GMI Cloud, B200 is in pre-order, so today this is a reservation plan rather than capacity you can launch.

NVIDIA Blackwell on GMI Cloud, including B200, is in pre-order and coming soon, and the GPU page lists B200 pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour. What you can settle now is the plan: the shape of each pool, the handoff between them, and how the reservation is split. H100 and H200 are available now, so the two-pool workflow can be tested on H200 while the B200 reservation is arranged.

...

| | Fine-tuning pool | Inference pool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main memory cost | Gradients, optimizer states, activations | Weights at serving precision, KV cache |
| Parallel layout | Expert parallelism inside the node, sharded data or pipeline parallelism across nodes | Experts spread across one replica, many identical replicas |
| Sized by | The largest planned run | Steady peak traffic plus one replica for swaps |
| Usage rhythm | Periodic, idle between runs | Always on |
| GMI Cloud product | Managed GPU Cluster or Bare Metal GPU | Prime Inference dedicated endpoint |
| Billing shape | Pay as you go (billed by the minute) or prepaid for clusters | Hourly per GPU, or reserved seasonally or annually |

...

The two pools have different usage rhythms, so they should not carry the same commitment. The inference pool runs all the time and is the natural candidate for reserved capacity. For B200, which is in pre-order, the reservation term is something you negotiate into the pre-order. Prime Inference offers reserved capacity on a seasonal or annual basis at lower per-hour rates, and there is no minimum contract for on-demand use. The fine-tuning pool is only busy some of the time. Compare pay-as-you-go by the minute with a prepaid cluster by estimating how many hours per month your runs actually take. GMI Cloud pricing is built for this kind of progression: start on demand, then move to dedicated or committed deployments as a workload stabilizes, with commitment structures matched to long-term utilization.

results.title: Like-for-Like Quotes on Managed B200, B300, and NVL72 Capacity
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

...

For managed HGX B200 and B300 clusters, send the RFQ to Together AI and Nebius, which both publicly list HGX B300 alongside managed Kubernetes, and to AWS for P6-B200 and P6-B300, where the managed layer has to be confirmed separately. For NVL72, include CoreWeave, Together AI, and Nebius, which quotes NVL72 on request. Put GMI Cloud on the list as well: GMI prices GPUs per GPU-hour, with networking and storage provisioned separately based on the workload, and all NVIDIA Blackwell hardware on GMI Cloud is currently in pre-order. Our managed clusters list H200 and B200 node types today. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 are pre-order GPU platforms, and whether an NVL72 reservation includes a managed layer, and how far it goes, is set in the pre-order quote rather than in the current cluster catalog. B300 is a hardware option on Prime Inference, our dedicated inference service, and like the rest of our Blackwell lineup it is in pre-order. The comparison only holds once every quote uses the same unit, GPU count, and scope.

...

## How GMI Cloud answers the RFQ

Managed GPU Cluster provides fully managed, Kubernetes-based multi-node GPU clusters for distributed training and large-scale inference, with centralized cluster lifecycle management. It's in early access. Managed clusters list H200 and B200 node types, with B200 in pre-order like the rest of our Blackwell lineup. GMI provisions and operates these clusters inside GMI-operated data centers, with deployment across the US, APAC, and EU.

For the Blackwell rows of the RFQ:

- HGX B200. B200 is pre-order, and the GPU page lists pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour. B200 is one of the listed node types for managed clusters.
- NVL72. GB200 NVL72 is pre-order, and the GPU pricing page lists pricing from $8.00 per GPU-hour. GB300 NVL72 is also pre-order, with pricing through our sales team. NVL72 is not among the published managed-cluster node types, so ask whether the managed layer is included, which layers it covers, and the billing unit behind the rate, and get all three in writing.
- B300. B300 is a hardware option on Prime Inference, our dedicated single-tenant inference service, where it's listed with 288 GB of HBM3e per GPU, and like the rest of our Blackwell lineup it is in pre-order. Prime bills per GPU-hour, with reserved capacity available seasonally or annually at lower hourly rates. That makes it a fair comparison for B300 inference capacity but not for a managed B300 training cluster, which should be quoted by providers that list HGX B300.

The pricing structure fits the RFQ. GPU pricing is per GPU-hour and covers compute, while networking and storage are provisioned separately based on your workload. Committed usage plans are discounted compared with on-demand pricing. When you request a managed cluster in the console, the form offers pay-as-you-go billing, charged by the minute with no upfront cost, and clusters are billed either pay as you go or prepaid. You also choose the data center, Kubernetes version, worker node type, node count, and OS image. The summary panel then shows the estimated monthly cost as list price, discount, and estimated total. The Managed GPU Clusters documentation walks through the form. Requests aren't processed automatically: after submitting, contact support to activate the cluster. Additional nodes on an existing cluster go through Node Requests.

results.title: Which Cloud Providers Rent Dedicated B200 Servers to Skip a Data Center Upgrade?
results.author: Colin Mo
highlights:
September 25, 2026

Choose a provider that rents B200 as single-tenant bare metal inside data centers it operates itself, so power and cooling for those servers sit with the provider instead of becoming a facilities project on your side, and hardware replacement terms go into the order. The server should still behave like one of your own: full root access, your OS image, local NVMe, RDMA between nodes, and a network path back to the racks you keep. That is the model behind GMI Cloud's Bare Metal GPU: dedicated physical servers with full root access and hardware-level control, predictable and isolated GPU performance, and SLA-backed delivery, all running inside GMI-operated data centers.

On timing: NVIDIA Blackwell on GMI Cloud, including B200, is in pre-order and coming soon; the GPU page lists B200 pricing from $5.00 per GPU-hour. The decision in front of you now is a reservation plan, not a same-day launch. H100 and H200 are available now, which lets your team profile workloads and test the bare-metal workflow while the B200 reservation is arranged.

...

On pricing structure, our GPU pricing supports both paths: on-demand billing for flexibility and committed usage plans with discounts for sustained workloads. Usage-adaptive pricing lets teams start on demand and move to dedicated or committed deployments as workloads stabilize, without forcing an early long-term commitment. For this plan, that means starting on demand on H100 or H200 today and moving to a committed B200 reservation, since B200 is in pre-order rather than on-demand capacity.

...

How soon can we start? H100 and H200 are available now, so onboarding, image preparation, and profiling can begin immediately. Confirm B200 delivery timing in the pre-order quote.
